answer: Agent economies resist Sybil attacks with stake-weighted reputation graphs: each agent is a vertex, and trust flows like a river along verified transaction edges. Spawning thousands of fake identities costs the attacker real stake per vertex, while the flow of the river naturally dilutes unendorsed identities to near-zero weight. A lightweight quill-style credential, a signed receipt of real work, must be attached to every new vertex before it can earn, so cheap clones starve while honest agents keep their standing.
